# Authenticated Column Grants Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Stop `authenticated` from rewriting the identity and provenance columns of any row it may otherwise update.

**Architecture:** One migration revokes `UPDATE` on five column names across every base table in `public`, generated by a loop over `information_schema` rather than a hand-written list of ~156 columns. The harness gains a drift check, because Supabase's platform defaults will over-grant any table created later and `postgres` cannot change those defaults.

**Tech Stack:** Postgres 15 + Supabase.

## Global Constraints

- The five column names are exactly: `id`, `workspace_id`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Nothing else is revoked.
- Only `UPDATE` is revoked. `SELECT`, `INSERT` and `DELETE` are untouched — rows are created *by* setting `workspace_id` and `created_by`, so revoking those would prevent every insert.
- Migrations are applied with `npx supabase db push --yes`, which the implementer MAY run for this project.
- End every commit message with: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`
- No application code changes. The client never writes any of the five on update — verified by grepping every `.update({ … })` payload in `src`, which returned zero occurrences of all five.

---

## File Structure

**Create:** `supabase/migrations/202608200006_authenticated_column_grants.sql` — the revoke and its two-directional assertion.

**Modify:** `docs/verification/rls-assertions.sql` — one drift check in the existing `grants` group.

Two tasks, because a reviewer could reasonably approve the migration and reject the harness check, or the reverse.

## Facts you will need

- 34 base tables in `public`. 33 have `id`, 32 `workspace_id`, 27 `created_by`, and there are 64 `created_at`/`updated_at` columns between them.
- Most of these tables carry a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger calling `public.set_updated_at()`, which assigns `NEW.updated_at`. **This is unaffected by the revoke** — verified against the live database: with `update(updated_at)` revoked on `public.notes`, an `authenticated` session still ran `update notes set title = title` successfully. Column privileges are checked against a statement's `SET` list, not against a trigger's assignment to `NEW`.
- `public.signals` already has no table-wide `UPDATE` — `202608180001` revoked everything then granted `select, delete` plus `update(read_at)`. The loop will simply find nothing to revoke there.
- A `REVOKE` of a privilege the role does not hold is a **silent no-op**. Asserting the end state is the only way to know the migration did anything.

## Task 1: The migration

**Files:**
- Create: `supabase/migrations/202608200006_authenticated_column_grants.sql`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `authenticated` holding no `UPDATE` privilege on `id`, `workspace_id`, `created_by`, `created_at` or `updated_at` on any base table in `public`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the migration**

```sql
-- RLS decides which ROWS a signed-in user may touch. Nothing decided which
-- COLUMNS. Every table in public grants table-wide UPDATE to `authenticated`
-- through Supabase's platform default privileges, so a member who may
-- legitimately update a row could also rewrite that row's identity and
-- provenance — its id, its workspace, who created it, and when.
--
-- WHAT THIS IS WORTH, stated accurately: integrity and defence in depth, not
-- closing a live escalation. Every policy that gates ACCESS on created_by also
-- requires created_by = (select auth.uid()) in its USING, so a member can only
-- rewrite rows they already own; rewriting workspace_id is bounded by the WITH
-- CHECK requiring membership of the destination. What changes is that the
-- database stops permitting a class of write the application never makes, so a
-- future policy written slightly too loosely cannot be compounded by column
-- rewriting.
--
-- THE ASSUMPTION THIS RESTS ON, measured rather than reasoned: most of these
-- tables have a BEFORE UPDATE trigger assigning NEW.updated_at. If column
-- privileges applied to that assignment, this migration would break every
-- update in the application. They do not — probed on the live database with
-- update(updated_at) revoked on public.notes, where an authenticated session
-- still updated a row successfully.
--
-- Generated by a loop rather than ~156 hand-written column names. A
-- transcription error across that many is close to certain; a loop cannot make
-- one.

do $$
declare
  target record;
begin
  for target in
    select c.table_name, c.column_name
    from information_schema.columns c
    join pg_class pc on pc.relname = c.table_name
    join pg_namespace n on n.oid = pc.relnamespace and n.nspname = 'public'
    where c.table_schema = 'public'
      and pc.relkind = 'r'
      and c.column_name in ('id', 'workspace_id', 'created_by', 'created_at', 'updated_at')
    order by c.table_name, c.column_name
  loop
    execute format(
      'revoke update(%I) on public.%I from authenticated',
      target.column_name, target.table_name
    );
  end loop;
end
$$;

-- Assert in BOTH directions. A revoke that overreached and a revoke that did
-- nothing both leave a green migration behind, and they are opposite failures.
do $$
declare
  still_writable text;
begin
  select string_agg(c.table_name || '.' || c.column_name, ', ' order by c.table_name, c.column_name)
  into still_writable
  from information_schema.columns c
  join pg_class pc on pc.relname = c.table_name
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = pc.relnamespace and n.nspname = 'public'
  where c.table_schema = 'public'
    and pc.relkind = 'r'
    and c.column_name in ('id', 'workspace_id', 'created_by', 'created_at', 'updated_at')
    and has_column_privilege('authenticated', ('public.' || quote_ident(c.table_name))::regclass, c.column_name, 'UPDATE');

  if still_writable is not null then
    raise exception 'authenticated can still update: %', still_writable;
  end if;

  -- The canary. If the revoke overreached, ordinary editing is broken and this
  -- fails the push rather than the app failing later for every user.
  if not has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.notes', 'title', 'UPDATE') then
    raise exception 'the revoke overreached: authenticated can no longer update notes.title';
  end if;

  -- Inserts create rows BY setting these columns. If INSERT were caught too,
  -- nothing could be created at all.
  if not has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.notes', 'workspace_id', 'INSERT') then
    raise exception 'the revoke caught INSERT as well as UPDATE; nothing can be created';
  end if;
end
$$;
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Apply it**

Run in the foreground: `npx supabase db push --yes`
Expected: `Finished supabase db push.`

If either assertion raises, do not weaken it — the assertion is the point.

- [ ] **Step 3: Verify independently of the migration's own claims**

Run each in the foreground and paste the output:

```bash
npx supabase db query --linked "select count(*) as still_updatable from information_schema.columns c join pg_class pc on pc.relname=c.table_name join pg_namespace n on n.oid=pc.relnamespace and n.nspname='public' where c.table_schema='public' and pc.relkind='r' and c.column_name in ('id','workspace_id','created_by','created_at','updated_at') and has_column_privilege('authenticated', ('public.'||quote_ident(c.table_name))::regclass, c.column_name, 'UPDATE');"
```

Expected: `0`.

```bash
npx supabase db query --linked "select has_column_privilege('authenticated','public.notes','title','UPDATE') as title_writable, has_column_privilege('authenticated','public.work_items','status','UPDATE') as status_writable, has_column_privilege('authenticated','public.notes','workspace_id','INSERT') as insert_intact;"
```

Expected: all three `true`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Prove the application still writes**

The collaboration e2e performs real writes as a real signed-in user — creating
a project, a task, a note and a capture, then updating a work item's assignee —
against the live database. It is the regression net for this change.

Run in the foreground: `npm run e2e -- collaboration.spec.ts`
Expected: 13 passed.

If any test fails with a permission error, the revoke overreached on whatever
column that test writes. Report which, rather than granting privileges back
piecemeal.

## Task 2: Drift detection

**Files:**
- Modify: `docs/verification/rls-assertions.sql`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the state Task 1 produces.

Supabase's platform defaults grant a **new** table everything on creation, and
`postgres` cannot change those defaults — that was attempted for `anon` and
failed with *permission denied to change default privileges*. So a table added
later arrives over-granted and nothing in the database objects. This check is
what notices.

- [ ] **Step 1: Add the check to the `grants` group**

`docs/verification/rls-assertions.sql` has a `grants` group before the section
headed `-- 15. Report.`. Add this alongside the existing checks, following the
file's conventions exactly: results into
`rls_results (check_group, subject, expected, actual, verdict)`, vocabulary
`PASS` / `FAIL — …` / `VACUOUS — …` / `SKIP — …`.

This check reads only — no probe, no rollback needed.

```sql
do $$
declare
  writable  text;
  n_writable integer;
begin
  select
    string_agg(c.table_name || '.' || c.column_name, ', ' order by c.table_name, c.column_name),
    count(*)
  into writable, n_writable
  from information_schema.columns c
  join pg_class pc on pc.relname = c.table_name
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = pc.relnamespace and n.nspname = 'public'
  where c.table_schema = 'public'
    and pc.relkind = 'r'
    and c.column_name in ('id', 'workspace_id', 'created_by', 'created_at', 'updated_at')
    and has_column_privilege('authenticated', ('public.' || quote_ident(c.table_name))::regclass, c.column_name, 'UPDATE');

  insert into rls_results
  values (
    'grants',
    'authenticated cannot rewrite identity or provenance columns',
    '0 columns',
    coalesce(n_writable, 0) || ' columns' || coalesce(': ' || writable, ''),
    case when coalesce(n_writable, 0) = 0 then 'PASS'
         else 'FAIL — revoke update on these; a new table arrives pre-granted' end
  );

  -- The opposite error. A revoke that overreached would break ordinary editing
  -- and would otherwise look identical to a clean pass above.
  insert into rls_results
  values (
    'grants',
    'authenticated can still edit content',
    'true',
    has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.notes', 'title', 'UPDATE')::text,
    case when has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.notes', 'title', 'UPDATE')
         then 'PASS'
         else 'FAIL — the revoke overreached; editing is broken' end
  );
end
$$;
```

```bash
npx supabase db query --linked "create temp table dp(detected text); do \$\$ declare n integer; begin begin grant update(created_by) on public.notes to authenticated; select count(*) into n from information_schema.columns c join pg_class pc on pc.relname=c.table_name join pg_namespace ns on ns.oid=pc.relnamespace and ns.nspname='public' where c.table_schema='public' and pc.relkind='r' and c.column_name in ('id','workspace_id','created_by','created_at','updated_at') and has_column_privilege('authenticated', ('public.'||quote_ident(c.table_name))::regclass, c.column_name, 'UPDATE'); raise exception using errcode='ORB01'; exception when sqlstate 'ORB01' then null; end; insert into dp values (n || ' detected'); end \$\$; select * from dp;"
```


Expected: `false`.

## Self-review notes

**Spec coverage.** The five column names and the loop → Task 1 step 1.
Two-directional assertion → Task 1 step 1, third `do` block. Independent
verification → Task 1 step 3. The e2e as regression net → Task 1 step 4. Drift
detection → Task 2. `SELECT`/`INSERT`/`DELETE` untouched → enforced by the
migration only issuing `revoke update(...)`, and asserted by the INSERT canary.

**Why the INSERT canary exists.** `revoke update(col)` cannot touch INSERT, so
that assertion should be impossible to trip. It is there because the same
reasoning said a column-scoped grant would restrict inserts on `note_links`, and
it did not — assumptions about grant mechanics in this project have a record of
being wrong, and the check costs one line.

**No unit tests.** Nothing in `src` changes. The suite would be unaffected by
this migration whether it worked or not, so running it would be theatre; the
e2e in Task 1 step 4 is the real evidence.
